subject: physics_2
question_text: Does the principle of conservation of energy hold for interference and diffraction phenomena? Explain briefly.

verification.note: The 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: I = 4I₀ cos²(φ/2) runs from 0 to 4I₀; the average of cos²(φ/2) over a cycle is 1/2, so the average intensity is 2I₀, exactly the sum I₀ + I₀ of the two waves acting separately — energy is redistributed between dark and bright fringes with no gain or loss, and the same argument applies to diffraction maxima and minima.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.
insider_note: The average intensity 2I₀ equalling I₀ + I₀ IS the answer — write that comparison explicitly, not just the word redistributed.

steps.label: The intensity pattern
lines: Two coherent waves, each of intensity I₀,
meet at a point P with phase difference φ.
The resultant intensity at P is
Bright fringe: I = 4I₀. Dark fringe: I = 0.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Set up the pattern: the intensity swings between 0 and 4I₀ as φ changes across the screen.
steps.why: The question is about where the energy goes, so the answer must start from how the energy is arranged: the formula shows some points receive 4I₀ and others receive nothing. That is the apparent problem the next steps resolve.
common_mistakes: Writing the maximum as 2I₀. Amplitudes add before squaring: (a + a)² = 4a², so the bright fringe is 4I₀.

recall.must_convey: That two waves of intensity I₀ each give I = 4I₀ cos²(φ/2), running from 0 at dark fringes to 4I₀ at bright fringes.

steps.memory_tip: Two I₀ waves make fringes from 0 up to 4I₀ — remember the two extremes.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. One line of averaging: the mean of cos² over a cycle is 1/2.
steps.why: Conservation is settled by the average over the whole screen, not by any single point. Averaging cos²(φ/2) over a full cycle of φ gives 1/2, so the screen as a whole receives 2I₀ — this number is what gets compared in the next step.
common_mistakes: Averaging cos(φ/2) instead of cos²(φ/2). The average of the cosine itself is zero; the average of its square is 1/2.

recall.must_convey: That the average of cos²(φ/2) over a cycle is 1/2, so the average intensity is 2I₀.
accept: average of cos squared is half
reject: energy missing from the dark fringes

steps.memory_tip: cos² averages to 1/2 over a cycle — half of 4I₀ is 2I₀.

steps.label: Energy is redistributed
steps.mark_note: 2I₀ = I₀ + I₀, no gain or loss
lines: Two waves acting separately would give
I₀ + I₀ = 2I₀ — exactly the average of the
pattern. The energy missing from the dark
fringes appears in the bright fringes.
There is no gain and no loss of energy.
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The comparison line — average with interference = sum without interference — is the actual argument.
steps.why: Conservation is shown by comparing the same light with and without interference: both give 2I₀ over the screen. Interference therefore only moves energy from the dark places to the bright places; it creates and destroys nothing.
common_mistakes: Saying the waves destroy each other at the dark fringes. The energy is not destroyed — it is found in the bright fringes.
Stating redistribution without the 2I₀ comparison that proves it.

recall.must_convey: That 2I₀ equals what the two waves would give separately, so interference only redistributes energy from dark fringes to bright fringes.
accept: same as the two waves acting separately
energy moves from dark to bright
reject: the average of cos squared is half

steps.memory_tip: With interference: average 2I₀. Without: I₀ + I₀ = 2I₀. Equal — so nothing was made or lost.

So the principle of conservation of energy
holds for both interference and diffraction.
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. The question names BOTH phenomena — answer for diffraction as well, then give the one-line yes.
steps.why: A diffraction pattern is also a set of maxima and minima made by superposition, so the same argument transfers: the pattern rearranges the incident energy without changing its total. The question asks does it hold — the answer must end with a clear yes.
common_mistakes: Answering only for interference. The question names diffraction too, and the concluding sentence must cover both.
Ending without a direct answer. Write the yes explicitly.

recall.must_convey: That the same redistribution argument applies to diffraction, so conservation of energy holds for both phenomena.

steps.memory_tip: Both patterns are superposition patterns — one argument answers both.
